questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Advanced Dependency Injection”?
options: Advanced Dependency Injection means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Advanced Dependency Injection removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Advanced Dependency Injection should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Advanced Dependency Injection helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Advanced Dependency Injection helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Advanced Dependency Injection is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Custom injection tokens” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Custom injection tokens” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Custom injection tokens” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Custom injection tokens” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Custom injection tokens” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Custom injection tokens” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Custom injection tokens” under Advanced Dependency Injection. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Advanced Dependency Injection”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
